text: The retirement date for Bittern-9 is August 19, 2027; after that day it stops serving.
Unlike Kestrel-8, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Bittern-9 is the Lattice team. Nobody should assume the owner of Bittern-9 applies to Kestrel-8, the owner differs.
Unlike Kestrel-8, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Lark-9 is Zig. Nobody should assume the language of Lark-9 applies to Kestrel-8, the language differs.
Source for Swift-4 is written in Rust; no other language is allowed in its repository.
Lark-9 enforces a rate limit of 3900 requests per minute per caller. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
Plan around the retirement date of Lark-9: November 3, 2027 is when it goes dark. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
Bittern-9 listens on port 8315; anyone who cannot reach that port should check the firewall rules.
Source for Kestrel-8 is written in Go; no other language is allowed in its repository. The entry was reformatted last quarter.

Unlike Egret-2, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Kestrel-8 is $550k. Nobody should assume the budget of Kestrel-8 applies to Egret-2, the budget differs. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
The service Merlin-6 takes traffic on port 9137, and the port is fixed across every environment.

Unlike Merlin-6, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Egret-2 is 1200 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Egret-2 applies to Merlin-6, the rate limit differs. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
Unlike Bittern-9, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Egret-2 is $1155k. Nobody should assume the budget of Egret-2 applies to Bittern-9, the budget differs.
Questions about Merlin-6 start with its owner, the Keystone team; they triage anything filed against it. An older draft of this note was archived.
Bittern-9 enforces a rate limit of 850 requests per minute per caller.
Hana Ekwueme is on the pager rotation of Egret-2 this month, with a deputy as backup.
Unlike Lark-9, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Merlin-6 is 400 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Merlin-6 applies to Lark-9, the rate limit differs.
Finance fixed the budget of Lark-9 at $2965k, reviewed every quarter.
All instances of Kestrel-8 live in the datacenter at Tallinn.
Egret-2 reaches its retirement date on July 9, 2029, so every consumer has to migrate before then.
Gideon Quintero is on the pager rotation of Lark-9 this month, with a deputy as backup.
Pages from Merlin-6 land on the pager rotation of Celia Castellan before anyone else.
The service Swift-4 takes traffic on port 6955, and the port is fixed across every environment.
Unlike Kestrel-8, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Swift-4 is $4655k. Nobody should assume the budget of Swift-4 applies to Kestrel-8, the budget differs.
Unlike Merlin-6, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Egret-2 is the Harbor team. Nobody should assume the owner of Egret-2 applies to Merlin-6, the owner differs.
The pager rotation for Kestrel-8 is run by Gideon Halvorsen; alerts page them first.
The primary datacenter of Swift-4 is Oslo; failover is handled by operations.
Plan around the retirement date of Merlin-6: May 5, 2028 is when it goes dark. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.

Unlike Bittern-9, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Swift-4 is December 1, 2029. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Swift-4 applies to Bittern-9, the retirement date differs.
Unlike Bittern-9, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Kestrel-8 is the Ledger team. Nobody should assume the owner of Kestrel-8 applies to Bittern-9, the owner differs.
Bittern-9 was granted a budget of $4160k this year; an unspent budget does not roll over.
